title: skills (automation): three texts still teach that a `connector_action` node's `connectorConfig.input` is sent as written; after #27327 it is evaluated like every other value slot
body:
domain:server#3 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4czuTWNgKR22fKv7jia

Filing gate: ① skills text that will contradict the runtime at named locations. Found by the #27327 card thread (PR #27980) and filed by the `domain:server` seat, because the skills tree is outside the server lane's surface. ⛔ Not a claim.

## Drift (lands with PR #27980)

PR #27980 (#27327) makes the executor evaluate `connector_action`'s `connectorConfig.input` through the shared `value-slot-map`, like `subflow`/`map` input, `script` inputs, `screen` defaults, `notify` templateData and the `http` body. An expression envelope there now resolves against the flow's variables; a constant payload is unchanged. These texts still teach the old limit, that the input is sent as written:

1. `skills/objectstack-automation/references/integration-recipes.md:18`
2. `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md:88`
3. `skills/objectstack-automation/evals/integrations-declared.json:7`

## Wanted

Re-teach the slot as an evaluated value slot in the same words the skill uses for its siblings. Include one example that reads a record field into the connector input. The eval's expectation follows. Also name the registration gap that #27968 tracks: until it lands, registration does not judge this slot, so a malformed envelope fails the step at run time instead of being refused at `os validate`.

⛔ Do not edit before PR #27980 merges. Until then the texts are still true.

## Dedupe

#27327 / PR #27980 (executor), #27968 (registration half), #27322 (the recipes that taught the limit). No open skills card covers these lines.
